newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia, Australia to develop eastern islands.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia, Australia to develop eastern islands.

text.p: Indonesia and Australia agreed on Friday to expand economic cooperation for the development of Indonesia's eastern islands, including the tourist haven Bali.

"The Australian and Indonesian governments have agreed to establish sub-regional economic cooperation under the name of AIDA (Australia-Indonesia Development Area)," Australian Foreign Minister Alexander Downer told reporters after meeting President Suharto.

"We see the initiative as a very constructive one. We believe there is very great potential to develop our economic cooperation, in particular in the area of tourism and the development of transport links and general business activities," Downer said.
Indonesia's coordinating minister of production and distribution, Hartarto (Eds: one word), welcomed the agreement for the development of Indonesia's eastern islands, including Bali.
"This is an initiative which is another example, and very important example, of the strengthening relationship between Australia and Indonesia," Downer said.
"We will establish a special working group which will involve people from the private sector and will be given the task of identifying areas where there is scope for substantial cooperation."
Hartarto said the private sector, including the mining industry, should play a major role in development. He said Indonesian investment would also be welcome in Australia.

While Indonesia's most populous island of Java has experienced high economic growth in recent years, islands in the eastern part of the archipelago still require major development to raise living standards.
The agreement was announced on the second day of a two-day Australia-Indonesia ministerial forum focused on economic relations in which six ministers from Canberra were participating.
